To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
neurotrophic factors signal through the activation of a number of receptor tyrosine kinases and their respective downstream signal transducers.

(1) neurotrophic factors signal through a number of receptor tyrosine kinases, (2) the receptors are activated by ligand binding, (3) the receptors activate the Ras pathway, and (4) the Ras pathway activates transcription factors.

neurotrophic factor-induced activation of the Ras/Raf/MEK/ERK pathway leads to the phosphorylation and activation of the cAMP-response-element-binding protein, which is a transcription factor involved in the regulation of the expression of genes encoding proteins that are involved in the control of cell survival.

the identification of signalling pathways and the characterization of their molecular components that are involved in the neurotrophin-induced differentiation of these neuronal and non-neuronal cells.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms by which neurotrophic factors exert their biological actions.
the elucidation of the intracellular pathways activated by neurotrophic factors and the mechanisms of action of these factors in neuronal and glial survival and differentiation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
neurotrophic factors activate the Trk receptors to activate the MAPK pathway and to induce cell survival.

these factors signal via a common receptor, the Trk family of receptor tyrosine kinases, to activate a variety of intracellular pathways that include the Ras/Raf/MAP kinase, phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI 3-kinases)/Akt and phospholipase C (PLC)/protein kinase C (PKC) pathways.

the neurotrophins, the glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF), and the insulin-like growth factors (IGFs) are able to activate the Ras-MAPK signalling pathway in a manner that is dependent upon receptor dimerization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neurotrophic factor receptor activation is a highly dynamic process.

neurotrophic factors, such as brain derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), neurotrophin 3 (NT3), neurotrophins 4/5 (NT4/5) and neurotrophin-6 (NT6), signal by binding to a single receptor, the TrkA, TrkB and TrkC receptor tyrosine kinase, and the p75 neurotrophin receptor.

the signalling cascades initiated by neurotrophin receptors, the neurotrophic tyrosine kinase receptors and the low-affinity p75 neurotrophin receptor, are remarkably similar, and are mediated by a common set of signalling molecules, which include the Ras GTPases, the phosphatidylinositol-3 kinase and the mitogen-activated protein kinases.
